html:
Awngthim is the language of the Winduwinda people, an Aboriginal people of the west coast of Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, around present day Weipa and Mapoon.

This coast saw the first recorded European landing in Australia. In 1606 the Dutch ship Duyfken under Willem Janszoon charted the Cape York shore and its crew clashed with local people. Neighbours on the map include the Wik peoples to the south and the Anggamudi to the north.

A Presbyterian mission was founded at Mapoon in 1891. From the 1960s bauxite mining at Weipa took over much of the land. The Awngthim language is now extinct. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: Awngthim is the language of the Winduwinda people, an Aboriginal people of the west coast of Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, around present day Weipa and Mapoon.
